capabilities.target: executive's drive: board materials and draft financial results
any email recipient (meeting attendees), sent from the executive's mailbox
calendar invite acceptance and prep-note drafting workflow

inputs.source: Calendar invite from any external sender; description field is free text authored by the sender.
The executive's own direct chat requests.

instructions.note: 'find related documents' places no limit on what is searched in the executive's drive, which holds board materials and draft financial results.
'email a short brief to the attendees' is treated as standing authorization to send drive content to whoever the invite lists as an attendee, with no check on who added them.

elements.name: Any external party who can send the executive a calendar invite
Executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)
Email recipients (invite attendees), possibly including the invite's own sender

controls.name: Daily summary review by the executive
controls.decay_rationale: The summary is generated by the same model that performed the actions, after the actions already completed. A more capable model can write a more persuasive, selectively incomplete summary (ASI09), and detection happens too late to prevent harm in any case.

controls.name: Human approval gate before mail.send on invite-triggered briefs
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented in the current design. If added as a raw-action, low-volume gate, it would be enforced outside the model and would not decay with model capability alone, though it would still depend on approval volume staying low.

controls.name: Recipient domain allowlist on mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. If added, it would make attacker-controlled external destinations unreachable by mail.send regardless of model behavior, unless the destination domain is separately pre-approved.

controls.name: Isolate invite free text from action-triggering logic
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Even if enforced in the orchestration layer rather than the prompt, a sufficiently capable model may still find ways to let invite metadata (e.g., attendee lists) steer behavior, so this narrows rather than fully severs the path.

controls.name: System-generated, tamper-evident audit log
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The only existing record (the daily summary) is written by the agent itself. A log generated directly from tool-call records, not model narration, would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Rate or step limit on invite-triggered actions
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; no limit on invite volume or triggered actions is stated anywhere in the design.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): invite-triggered drive read and unrestricted email send exfiltrates confidential documents to the invite's own sender

attack_path.note: Attacker sends a calendar invite; the description field is free text the attacker fully controls, and the attacker can list any address, including their own, as an attendee.
Agent accepts the invite (time is free) and starts the 'prepare' workflow driven by the invite's content and attendee list, with no human approval.
Agent searches and reads the executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results) to assemble the brief.
Agent emails the brief to 'the attendees' -- which includes the invite's own sender -- with no recipient restriction or approval step.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model or orchestration version change; any new drive/mail connector added; approval controls still absent after reassessment.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to accept invites and, for each one, search drive and email a brief to attendees, with no check on who the invite is from.
Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite; the invite description is free text written by the sender, so the triggering content is attacker-controlled.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results, i.e., restricted data reachable by drive_read.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, so the brief built from confidential drive content can be sent to any attendee, including the invite's own sender.

recommendations.action: Require a human approval gate (raw-action review showing the actual recipient list and content) before mail.send executes for any brief triggered by an invite from an untrusted or external sender.
Restrict mail.send recipients by default to the company's own email domain; require a separate explicit authorization step to add any external recipient.
Stop treating calendar invite free-text descriptions as instructions; isolate invite content so it can only supply scheduling metadata, never what is searched or sent.
Add an independently generated, tamper-evident audit log of every drive read and email sent, reviewable by someone other than the agent.

findings.title: No independent audit trail: the daily summary is self-reported by the agent (ASI09, repudiation)

forecast.watch_signal: Summary-generation prompt or model changes; absence of independent logging remains unaddressed at reassessment.

evidence.observation: The daily summary is written by the agent itself, so there is no independent, tamper-evident record of which documents were read or which emails were sent to whom.
The executive reviews a daily summary only after actions have already been taken, and that summary is model-generated rather than drawn from a system record.

recommendations.action: Replace or supplement the agent-authored daily summary with a system-generated log drawn directly from tool-call records, not from the model's own narration.

findings.title: No rate or step limit on invite-triggered actions enables resource exhaustion and repeated exfiltration (ASI08)

forecast.watch_signal: Observed volume of invites processed per day; absence of any stated rate or spend limit persists at reassessment.

evidence.observation: Agent acts on invites 'as they arrive' with no stated limit on volume or rate of invite processing.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, and no rate or spend limit is mentioned anywhere in the design.

recommendations.action: Add a rate or step limit on invite-triggered drive reads and email sends (for example, per sender, per hour), escalating to a human when exceeded.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe any authentication or identity verification mechanism for the agent process itself.
Artifacts do not state step or rate limits for the agent's invite-processing loop beyond what is captured in the rate-limit finding.
The sender is already treated as untrusted regardless of claimed identity; no differential privilege is granted based on sender identity in this design.
Artifacts do not describe any transport integrity protection (signing, encryption) for inbound calendar invites.
This is an inbound flow carrying only the attacker's invite content; it does not itself carry data leaving the organization.
Artifacts do not describe integrity protection for outbound email content in transit.
Artifacts do not describe write protections or integrity controls on the drive contents themselves.
Artifacts do not describe any read-rate limiting on the drive store independent of the overall invite-processing rate limit gap.
The daily summary is an internal report delivered only to the executive; it is not exposed to any additional party beyond the trust boundary already crossed.
The summary is produced once per day regardless of invite volume, so it cannot itself be flooded or exhausted by invite traffic.
The recipient address is taken directly from the calendar invite's attendee list; the relevant risk is that any sender can add themselves as attendee, not address spoofing.

rating.rationale: The untrusted calendar invite reaches, in sequence, a drive read of restricted board/financial materials and an unrestricted external email send (the lethal trifecta, TC1), with the invite's own sender legitimately listed as a recipient. No preventive control of any kind exists on this path -- no approval gate, no recipient restriction, no content isolation -- so residual equals inherent at critical. The only declared control (a daily, agent-written summary) is purely detective, acts after harm is already done, and is itself undermined by having no independent record (f2), so it earns no credit under rubric section 5 and does not lower the floor. A related property gap -- no stated rate or step limit on invite-triggered actions (f3) -- could amplify both exposure and resource cost. Because residual is already at the ceiling, no considered trigger raises the forecast further; the forecast stays critical and the system needs structural controls (approval gating, a recipient/domain allowlist, isolation of invite content from action-triggering logic, and an independent audit log) before any model or scope change should be treated as acceptable.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; the three capabilities (drive_read, mail_send, calendar_prepare) are inferred from prose descriptions, so exact credential scoping and transport security could not be independently verified.

Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes, spawning, self-configuration) are not stated in the artifacts and were treated as absent for inherent risk purposes; if undocumented limits exist, inherent risk could be lower than computed here.
